First, let's recall the double-angle formula for sine: 

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡2x=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x
$$

Substituting $x={30}^{∘}$ into the above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot {30}^{∘}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘} \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({60}^{∘}) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can rewrite the given expression using the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡{60}^{∘}\operatorname{cot}⁡{30}^{∘}-1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} & =\frac{2\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}}{\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}}-1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{2{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-1+{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-(1-{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}}\end{aligned}
$$

Using  the Pythagorean identity in the form ${sin}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}=1-{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-(1-{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} & =\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}-{sin}^{2}⁡{30}^{∘}}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘})(\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}} \\  & =\frac{(\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘})\cancel{(\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘})}}{\cancel{\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}-\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}}} \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡{30}^{∘}+\operatorname{sin}⁡{30}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$
